title: Kueper2024: Unilateral vs bilateral movement-execution EEG dataset
description: EEG recordings from 8 healthy participants performing self-initiated, self-paced reaching movements with either the right arm alone (unilateral) or both arms synchronously (bilateral). Data were acquired with a 64-channel wireless active-electrode system and support movement intention recognition for exoskeleton-supported stroke rehabilitation and brain-computer interface research. This BIDS release was produced via MOABB from the original Zenodo deposit.
methods_description: 64-channel EEG plus 3 auxiliary channels recorded with a Brain Products LiveAmp64 and Acticap slim active electrodes (extended 10-20 montage, reference FCz, ground AFz) at 500 Hz, with hardware prefiltering of 0.1-131 Hz. Each participant performed 3 sets of 40 self-initiated movements per condition (unilateral right-arm button press, bilateral synchronous arm movement), giving 6 runs per subject.
